chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend to depart during the two days, it is not permissible for you to depart until the sun declines; and if you delay until the last of the days of Tashreeq, which is the final day of departure, there is no blame upon you regarding which hour you depart and cast the stones, whether before or after midday.

So when you depart and reach Al-Hasbah, which is Al-Bat'ha, if you wish to stay a little, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father would stay there, then mount and enter Makkah without having slept in it.'

key_terms.التَّشْرِيق: The days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah) in Mina
key_terms.الزَّوَال: Solar noon / decline of the sun
key_terms.الْبَطْحَاء: Al-Bat'ha, another name for the area in Mina

ai.seo_question: What are the specific times and conditions for departing Mina during the days of Tashreeq according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the temporal flexibility of the 'Nafar' (departure) from Mina, distinguishing between the strict post-noon requirement for the first two days of Tashreeq and the unrestricted timing on the final day. It further highlights the Prophetic and Imami practice of resting briefly at Al-Bat'ha before entering Mecca, emphasizing the balance between ritual obligation and ease. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on following the specific timings established by the Ahl al-Bayt, which often provide greater leniency compared to other schools.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you intend to depart during the two days, so it is not upon you that you depart until the (start of the) decline of the sun; and if you were to delay it to the last day of Al-Tashreek, and it is the day of the departure, the last one, so it is not upon you which time you depart and pelt (the rocks), whether before the midday or after it.

So when you depart and end up to Al-Hasbat, and it is Al-Bat’ha, you can encamp a little if you so desire to, for Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> would encamp in it, then carry on, so he<sup>asws</sup> would enter Makkah from without have slept in it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If you like to depart in the first two days, you cannot depart before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime). If you delay until the last days of tashriq, which is the day of departure, then it does not matter in whatever hour you depart or throw pebbles, before or after Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime).

When you depart and arrive in al-Hasabah which is Batha’, you may disembark there for a little while.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would disembark there; then depart and enter Makkah without staying there for the night.’”
